body: Flag: SEVERE. Dewan Housing Finance (DHFL), once India's third-largest housing financier, collapsed in 2019 after the IL&FS-triggered funding freeze and a Cobrapost exposé (Jan-2019) alleging ~Rs 31,000 cr routed to shell companies. RBI superseded the board (Nov-2019); first NBFC resolved under IBC -- Piramal acquired it (Sep-2021); public equity was extinguished. Findings: SEBI's final order (12-Aug-2025, 181 pages) held that from 2006 to Mar-2019 DHFL promoters/executives diverted ~Rs 14,040 cr to 'Bandra Book Entities' (Wadhawan-linked firms) disguised as retail housing loans in a hidden branch-level book; it barred Kapil and Dheeraj Wadhawan for 5 years (Rs 27 cr fine each) and Rakesh and Sarang Wadhawan for 4 years (Rs 20.75 cr each), ~Rs 120 cr fines in all. CBI's ~Rs 34,926 cr bank-consortium fraud case (2022; UBI-led 17 banks) is in trial; the Supreme Court granted the brothers bail (Dec-2025) citing trial delay; a Delhi court refused CBI's plea to add charges (Oct-2026, single-source). The Yes Bank link: Yes Bank invested ~Rs 3,700 cr in DHFL debt in 2018 allegedly in return for ~Rs 600 cr loan to a Rana Kapoor family firm (CBI allegation). Wadhawans were earlier tied to HDIL/PMC Bank fraud. Early signals: loan growth far above peers with thin disclosure, large 'project loans' to opaque builders, wholesale funding mismatch, and an auditor/whistleblower trail.

data.regulator_findings: SEBI Aug-2025: Rs 14,040 cr diverted; bans and Rs ~120 cr fines
data.status_2026: criminal trial ongoing; brothers on bail (Dec-2025)
